item.title: Reverse to C: sum_sq (2026-09-22)
item.description:
Target: Windows x86-64 (MSVC calling convention: RCX = arg1, EDX = arg2). Reverse this function to equivalent C.
sum_sq: push rbp mov rbp, rsp xor eax, eax ; total = 0 xor r8d, r8d ; i = 0 .loop: cmp r8d, edx jge .done movsxd r9, dword ptr [rcx + r8*4] imul r9, r9 add rax, r9 inc r8d jmp .loop .done: pop rbp ret
What does sum_sq compute, and what are its parameter types?
--- Answer ---
long long sum_sq(int *arr, int count) { long long total = 0; for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) { long long v = arr[i]; total += v * v; } return total; }
Explanation: push rbp / mov rbp, rsp / pop rbp is a standard stack-frame prologue and epilogue; this function has no locals or callees, so RBP is only saved and restored, never dereferenced. movsxd r9, [rcx + r8*4] reads a 32-bit int at scaled index i and sign-extends it into a 64-bit register before squaring, matching arr[i] widened to long long. cmp r8d, edx / jge .done is the loop guard (i < count), and RAX (return register) accumulates the running sum of squares.
